The reservoir question

What happens
between the wells?

These views explain the intended mechanisms and the questions each test is designed to answer.

Contact and containment

Can injected fluid reach oil in the reservoir and remain in the intended area long enough to be useful? Actual pathways and pressure changes require field measurements and reservoir analysis.

Well-to-well communication

Nearby wells can respond to injection. Geometry helps show the setting, but proximity alone does not prove a connected flow path.

Incremental recovery

A post-injection production increase needs a defensible baseline and a view of the participating wells. The animations are explanations of a process, not forecasts of added barrels.

Measured history comes next

A foundation for comparison.

The first version connects project evidence with well geometry. Verified injection records, production histories and cycle dates can later support a measured timeline. Current animations do not encode those volumes.
